tasks.short: Manage production schedules and communication plans

steps.what: Submit dates for production staff
Create documentation and production schedules
Set prototyping goals in collaboration
Draft communication plans from the goals
Sign schedules, goals and communication plans
Manage the signed production schedules

tasks.design: The producer submits milestone date, owner and dependency on a {PROJECT} form. A {DOCS} template drafts the production schedules, the prototyping goals sheet and the communication plans from those fields. The game designer sets the goals with the producer and signs one pack. The board shows only the signed version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates lived in mail and the plan lived in a separate document, so a board could not tell a signed date from a wish.
tasks.enabler_now: A milestone can carry a date, an owner and a dependency that a schedule template can place.
tasks.still_hard: Which goal is realistic, and agreeing it with production staff, is a collaboration.
tasks.human_edge: The designer sets the prototyping goals and signs the schedule.

ambition.what: Reset prototyping goals each week with the producer, not only at the milestone

tasks.altitude: Less rewriting of plans. The designer can refuse a date that has no owner, and the collaboration on goals stays.

reach.task: Run the week from the signed production schedule
reach.learn: Which dates are signed and which prototyping goals are still blank

evidence.claim: Production schedules, documentation and communication plans in a mid-size studio have a stable shape. Agreeing a prototyping goal with production staff does not.
A template can place a date, an owner and a goal the designer already wrote. It cannot decide whether the goal is realistic.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer, in collaboration with the producer. The task ends when the signed pack is on the board. Doing the production work is later.

Input contract: milestone id, date, owner role, dependency id, prototyping goal text the designer wrote, audience for the communication plan. Producer of dates is the producer. Producer of goal text is the game designer. A date with no owner is rejected and not guessed.
Use the project board and the document templates that already exist before custom code. The spreadsheet prior is the date list. The meeting prior is the collaboration, which stays.
unknowns: Who may sign a schedule when the designer is away.
Which milestones have no single owner.
research_questions: What share of dates arrive with no owner?
How often does the signed goal differ from the producer's first date?

already_counted.description: Setting prototyping goals stays a collaboration
Designer corrects a date the template misplaced

incremental.description: Revise schedule and plan headings when a new milestone type appears
Producer resubmits dates the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: schedule pack signed for this milestone set

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes dates still arrive as free-text mail, so the schedule is retyped and the goal conversation is unchanged. The high case assumes the form is used, but setting prototyping goals and signing the pack stay manual. Production work itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge adherence and tell production staff

steps.what: Open the original design points
Judge technical qualities and adherence
Provide feedback to production staff
Hear the feedback on the design
Draft feedback regarding original design
Sign the adherence feedback note
File the signed adherence feedback

tasks.design: The original design points sit in {DOCS} with a design id. The game designer compares the build with those points and gives feedback to production staff in the room. A note quotes only the points the designer marked as met or missed. The designer signs the note. The note never changes a live build on its own.
tasks.previous_blocker: The original design and the build notes were separate, so feedback often cited a memory of the design rather than an id.
tasks.enabler_now: A design point can carry an id that a feedback note can cite as met or missed.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a miss is acceptable, and how to say it to production staff, is a judgement in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The designer judges adherence and the technical qualities.
tasks.altitude: The feedback meeting stays. The note cites design ids, and the designer can refuse a line that cites none.

reach.task: Fix only the misses the designer signed
reach.learn: Which design ids were marked missed and which were accepted

evidence.claim: Feedback to production staff on technical qualities and adherence is a meeting plus a short note. The judgement of the build stays with the designer.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so this note never changes a live build on its own.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed feedback note is filed. Changing the build is a later programmer task, done while a person watches.
Input contract: design id, original point text, build id, met or missed as marked by the designer, comment. Producer of the mark is the game designer. A line with no design id is dropped.
The meeting prior is accepted. Use the document store's own template before custom code. No unattended change to a live build.
unknowns: Who may sign adherence feedback when the designer is away.
Which original design points have no id.
research_questions: What share of feedback lines cite no design id?
How often does the signed note accept a miss the first mark had failed?

already_counted.description: Judging the build stays with the designer
Telling production staff stays a conversation

incremental.description: Keep the met-or-missed headings aligned with design ids

approvals.approved_version: adherence note signed for this build id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the original design has no stable ids, so the note is still written by hand and the meeting is unchanged. The high case assumes ids are clean, but judging the build and telling production staff stay manual. No unattended build change is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create gameplay prototypes and present them

steps.what: Create gameplay prototypes in the editor
Add a control the prototypes need
List presentation questions for the prototypes
Present prototypes to creative and technical staff
Sign the presentation note for management

tasks.design: The designer builds the gameplay prototypes by hand in the game editor ({OTHER}). A {DOCS} sheet lists the presentation from points the designer wrote: prototype id, the question to answer, and who must be in the room. The presentation to creative and technical staff stays a meeting. A note of what was decided is signed afterwards. The prototype itself is not generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prototype intent lived with the designer, so the presentation often showed a build without a written question.
tasks.enabler_now: A presentation can list a prototype id and a question the designer wrote, which a one-page note can carry.
tasks.still_hard: Making the prototype feel right, and reading the room, stays with the designer.
tasks.human_edge: The designer creates the prototypes and leads the presentation.
tasks.altitude: The build and the presentation stay manual. The one-page note is the only part that moves, and the designer can refuse a question they did not write.

reach.task: Support the prototype only where the designer asked
reach.learn: Which prototype id is being shown and which question it answers

evidence.claim: Gameplay prototypes and the presentation to staff and management are person work in a mid-size studio. A one-page question list is the small structured part.
A template can place a prototype id and a question the designer already wrote. It cannot build the prototype or run the presentation.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the presentation note is signed. The prototype remains a manual build.
Input contract: prototype id, question the designer wrote, audience role, build id. Producer is the game designer. If the question is empty the sheet stays blank.
The meeting prior is the presentation and is accepted. The build is screen work in the game editor. Use the document template that already exists before custom code. No model writes the prototype.
unknowns: Whether a programmer must be in the room for every prototype.
Who may sign the presentation note when the designer is away.
research_questions: What share of presentations have no written question?
How often is the prototype rebuilt after the presentation?

already_counted.description: Building the prototypes stays with the designer
The presentation stays in the room

incremental.description: Keep the presentation sheet headings aligned with prototype ids

approvals.approved_version: presentation note signed after this showing

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the question is not written down, so the note is typed afterwards and the build and presentation are unchanged. The high case assumes the one-page note is filled from fields, but creating the prototypes and presenting them stay manual. Later production work is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Guide design discussions and log the agreement

steps.what: Write questions for the design discussions
Guide design discussions between development teams
State a development constraint on the design
State an art constraint on the design
Sign the agreement from the discussions
File the signed discussions agreement

tasks.design: The designer writes the questions for a discussion on a {DOCS} page with a design id. The discussion between development teams stays in the room. The designer guides it and states the agreement in one sentence. A decision log quotes only that sentence and is signed. The log does not decide.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreements were spoken and then remembered differently by each team, because there was no single sentence tied to a design id.
tasks.enabler_now: An agreement can be one sentence plus a design id, which a log can quote without reinterpreting it.
tasks.still_hard: Guiding the discussion, and what the teams will accept, is people work.
tasks.human_edge: The designer guides the discussion and states what was agreed.
tasks.altitude: The discussion stays. The designer leaves with a signed sentence instead of three memories, and can reject a log line they did not say.

reach.task: Build only what the signed discussion agreed
reach.learn: Which design ids have an agreement and which are still open

evidence.claim: Guiding design discussions between development teams is a conversation. The decision log is a short quote of a sentence the designer stated.
A template can file one agreement sentence against a design id. It cannot guide the discussion or decide what the teams will accept.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when the signed decision log is filed. The discussion is not a system record while it happens.
Input contract: design id, question, agreement sentence the designer states, team role. Producer of the agreement sentence is the game designer. If they state nothing, the log stays empty.
The meeting prior is accepted. Use the document store's own template before custom code.
unknowns: Which teams must be in the room for a given design id.
Who may sign the log when the designer is away.
research_questions: What share of discussions end with no single agreement sentence?
How often do teams later disagree with the signed sentence?

already_counted.description: Guiding the discussions stays in the room
Designer rejects a log line they did not say

incremental.description: Keep the decision log headings aligned with design ids

approvals.approved_version: discussion agreement signed for this design id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes agreements stay spoken only, so the log is thin and the discussion is unchanged. The high case assumes the log quotes a stated sentence, but guiding the discussions and signing stay manual. Later build work is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Schedules and communication plans stop being rewritten by hand. Prototypes, production feedback and design discussions stay with the designer.
reach: Producers read a signed schedule and the prototyping goals instead of a mail thread.
Programmers hear production feedback that cites the original design id, and do not change a live build from an unsigned note.
skills_to_grow: Write a schedule as dates, owners and a prototyping goal a board can show.
Cite the original design id when judging whether a build still matches.
Keep a design discussion in the room and the agreement in one signed sentence.
role.ambitious_version: The week opens on a signed schedule, a prototype the designer still builds by hand, and a decision log from the last discussion.
